original.reason: It falsely claims every binomial coefficient \(\binom{n}{k}\) with \(0<k<n\) is divisible by \(n\). This is not true for general \(n\), so the key justification is invalid, even though the required divisibility does hold when \(n=p^r\).

judgment.reason: Correct induction from the freshman's dream for exponent \(p\).
The displayed step replacing \((a+b)^{p^{n-1}}\) by \(a^{p^{n-1}}+b^{p^{n-1}}\) is asserted without an induction argument or prior proof.
It establishes the exponent-\(p\) identity and explicitly applies it repeatedly, which proves the claim for every positive \(n\).
The required divisibility \(p\mid\binom{p^n}{i}\) for intermediate \(i\) is correctly invoked via the standard p-adic valuation fact, so the binomial expansion is valid.
